00Summary at a Glance

Read at the Oct 15, 02:00 KST live price: NVIDIA in a re-assess-after-conditions zone · AMD and Intel lean wait-and-see
All three stocks sold off intraday on Oct 14 (NVIDIA −2.8%, AMD −5.6%, Intel −3.5%, SOX −3.6%). September consumer price inflation (CPI) of 3.7% year on year, above the 3.6% expected, appears to be the backdrop, but no stock-specific catalyst was found. This year AMD (+167%) and Intel (+169%) have far outrun NVIDIA (+19.1%), but price relative to earnings is the reverse. NVIDIA's earnings grew faster than its share price, so it got cheaper, while AMD and Intel are priced as if post-2027 expectations were already delivered.
  • Fundamentals. NVIDIA's latest quarter: revenue of $96.2 bn (+106%), with next-quarter guidance of $108 bn. AMD: data center revenue +107%, next-quarter guidance of $13.0 bn. Intel: revenue +25%, a return to growth after four years, though the foundry unit lost $2.1 bn in the quarter.
  • Valuation pressure. Next-fiscal-year estimated P/E is 14.0x for NVIDIA (FY28E), 36.4x for AMD (2027E) and 47.5x for Intel (2027E). The decline lowered all three from the prior day, but the ranking is unchanged.
  • Timing. The Nasdaq is −3.4% from its high, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) is −19.7%, below its 60-day moving average (12,007); the US 10-year yield is 5.24% intraday. NVIDIA is below its 20-day moving average ($228.7) and above its 60-day ($219.8). AMD is below its 20-day MA and slipped intraday through both the open of the Sep 21 Dante base candle ($583.88) and the first support candidate ($575-584). Intel slipped intraday below even its 60-day MA ($101.7).
  • Next checkpoints. The Oct 14 regular-session close, TSMC earnings on Oct 15, the FOMC on Oct 28, Intel earnings on Oct 29 (confirmed), AMD earnings on Nov 3 (confirmed), and NVIDIA earnings after mid-November (date not announced).

01Who Makes What

All three companies sell "AI data center chips," but from different positions. NVIDIA sells systems that bundle GPUs with a software ecosystem, AMD sells the alternative, and Intel sells CPUs together with "chipmaking on US soil" (foundry services).

DesignNVIDIA (GPU, Rubin), AMD (GPU MI450, CPU EPYC), Intel (CPU Xeon)
Contract manufacturing
ManufacturingTSMC makes most of them. Intel uses its own 18A process and is also pursuing outside foundry customers
HBM pairing
AI servers and data centersMicrosoft, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and others. Some also develop their own chips

Does the "AI chip supercycle" reach all three equally?

No. Money is flowing overwhelmingly to NVIDIA right now, while AMD and Intel are being moved by expectations of money still to come.

  • NVIDIA: Revenue growth is above 100%, yet the stock is up only 19.1% this year. Earnings grew faster than the price, so trailing P/E fell from 45x (at the January fiscal year-end) to 28x (at the Oct 14 intraday live price), and to 23.9x on this year's estimates.
  • AMD: Most of its gigawatt-scale contracts start to appear in revenue from 2027. The current price assumes those contracts are delivered on schedule.
  • Intel: The core CPU business has revived on AI server demand, but the foundry unit lost $2.1 bn in the quarter and outside-customer revenue was only $290 million.
  • Easy to miss: NVIDIA said soaring memory prices could push its gross margin down to 71-72% in Q4. The memory boom covered in the Semiconductors ① report is a cost burden for GPU makers.

02Earnings and Outlook

NVIDIA's revenue is on a path to grow 7x in three years and AMD's to double in two, while Intel returns to growth in 2026 after four years of decline. Because GAAP earnings are not comparable across the three (Intel's one-off losses, for example), the annual comparison uses revenue.

Quarterly Trend: Who Is Accelerating

The difference in absolute scale is the key point. NVIDIA's one-quarter revenue increase (about $11.8 bn on guidance) is larger than AMD's entire quarterly revenue ($11.5 bn). AMD is growing fast, with Q2 revenue +50%, but the current price assumes MI450 volume shipments in 2027 go to plan. Intel's Q3 guidance ($15.8-16.8 bn) is similar to Q2 ($16.1 bn), so the Oct 29 report is the first test of whether Q2's sharp rebound continues (the date was confirmed by a company notice on Oct 6; the Oct 22 shown on earlier calendar sites was corrected).

NVIDIA's risk: customers become competitors

  • A single direct customer accounted for 16% of Q2 revenue.
  • Microsoft has secured a third-generation in-house AI chip, and Google's TPU is expanding external sales.
  • Still, Q3 guidance is +12% quarter on quarter, so no erosion has shown up in the numbers yet.

AMD's risk: executing its first rack system

  • Helios is AMD's first rack-scale system. It is entering ground NVIDIA has refined for years.
  • The OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic contracts total up to 14 GW. If the schedule slips, 2027 earnings estimates shift wholesale.
  • CEO Lisa Su said the company is "ahead of internal expectations."

Intel's risk: foundry customers

  • 18A output is about 25% above target and yields are improving.
  • But outside foundry revenue is $290 million per quarter, and no confirmed external 14A customer has been disclosed.
  • Capex burden, share dilution and a forecast decline in the 2026 PC market underpin the bearish case.

Analyst opinion counts are S&P Global figures (October). NVIDIA revenue is FY27E (Feb 2026 to Jan 2027); AMD and Intel are 2026E.

06Is the Price Cheap?

Relative to earnings, the cheapest of the three is the leader, NVIDIA. AMD and Intel's share prices this year have far outrun earnings growth, so even on 2027 earnings their P/E is about 36-48x (36.4x and 47.5x). The Oct 14 intraday decline lowered the multiples from the prior day, but the ranking is unchanged.

Unlike in Korea, where foreign and institutional daily net buying and selling data are published, US stocks have no such daily data, so volume is used as a proxy for selling intensity. The Oct 14 volume is a cumulative intraday figure (12:52 p.m. ET), so it cannot be compared directly with the prior day's final figure, and the 20-day and 60-day averages include this intraday bar. Falling on shrinking volume is read as a "pause" correction; falling on rising volume is read as a "dumping" decline.

Indicators are calculated from the last five years of daily bars (about 1,250 trading days), and the last bar is the Oct 14 intraday value. The weekly and monthly bars are built by aggregating the daily bars, so the latest week's and month's bars also contain intraday values. AMD's former Support 1 candidate ($575~584) became an upside resistance candidate after this intraday break.

How the Dante technique is reflected. "Dante" is the pen name of 주식단테, a Korean stock YouTuber known for chart-based methods built on long moving averages and "base candles" (large high-volume candles that mark institutional accumulation). This report marks both Dante's 112-, 224- and 448-day averages and the 122-, 244- and 444-day averages requested for the report, and searches the daily bars directly for the signals Dante cites as evidence of "institutional accumulation," attaching a checklist for each stock. There are five criteria. ① Base candle (accumulation candle): a bullish candle with volume at least 2x the prior 20-day average and a body of 3% or more. ② Base candle open as support: whether later closes hold above that candle's open (in the Dante technique this open is treated as the big players' average cost and the reference for judging a breakdown). ③ Volume dry-up after the high-volume candle: how far the 10-day average volume after the base candle falls relative to the base candle. ④ Time correction below the 224-day MA: whether a "bowl pattern" second leg (sideways for four months or more) exists. ⑤ Suspected breakdown candle: a long bearish candle with at least 2x volume within 15% of the 52-week high. The ▲ markers and dotted lines on the chart show base candles within the last 150 trading days and their opens (orange = still holding, gray = already broken). Because this edition's last bar is before the regular-session close, a "breakdown" is on an intraday basis; Dante's criterion, a close below the open, is only confirmed after the close. These criteria were quantified from secondary sources that summarize the technique, not from Dante's original videos, so they may differ from Dante's own judgment.
